name: take-in-the-world: the World seat
description: Brings the outside world in for a query: a web search through the selected search arm and, for research questions, the papers of the world-knowing seat. Returns an answer with the sources a reader can check.
purpose: Connect any AI to tools, search and data sources without writing code for each one.
approach: Admit tools and data sources through narrow interfaces and compare each candidate on the same tasks.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-take-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-take-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-take-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-take-in-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Task pass rate and cost per passing task, per hub.
outputs: Outside material for a task, from the search backends.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: reason-and-answer: the Mind seat
description: Asks a model for the answer to a prompt at a tier, using the model the tier chooser measured best for that tier. Planning and streaming live in the consumer.
purpose: Reason to a good answer at the lowest cost that still passes, for any product that needs an AI that plans and answers.
approach: Plan the steps, call the cheapest model tier that passes, and stream progress while the work runs.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-reason-and-answer has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-reason-and-answer has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-reason-and-answer chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Answer quality per dollar and per second.
parameters: A model-call seat and a tier-selection seat (built on first use, so a prompt with no tier never asks for it).
outputs: The text a model answers to the prompt at that tier.
effects: One model call per request, which costs what the provider charges or draws on the operator's subscription.
usage_notes: No arm yet: specified; implemented in Quest AI Runner, moving here.

name: choose-a-model-tier: pick the model for each tier
description: Picks, for each model tier, the provider and model that passes the most work per dollar on the same cases, counting prepaid credits as cost.
purpose: Choose the cheapest model that does the job at each tier, for any product that calls models.
approach: Rank each provider and model by passing work per cost on shared cases and the prices on file.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-choose-a-model-tier has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: The chosen model per tier passes the most work per dollar on shared cases.
parameters: bars: optional keyword arguments that set the quality bars.
inputs: tiers (tier name to candidate arms with cases run, cases passed and tokens), prices (rows from the price file), optional credits and defaults.
outputs: A mapping from each tier to the chosen provider and model.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: know-the-world: the Science seat
description: Looks up what the world says now and returns it as observations a reader can cite, weighing papers and data rather than a single web page.
purpose: Support claims with sources a reader can check, for anyone who asks an AI a factual or research question.
approach: Search the strongest sources available and return their findings as citable observations.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-know-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-know-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-know-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-know-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Claims supported by sources; evidence weighed.
parameters: The search-backend a search arm needs, an optional API key and contact address for the scholarly service, and a timeout.
inputs: One query or a list of queries with an optional result limit and a freshness flag; or a page address with an optional focus, part and full flag.
outputs: One observation: title, link and snippet per hit, or the passages of a page that bear on a focus; a failure comes back as an observation of kind error, never a raised exception.
effects: Makes network requests to the scholarly service or the web and keeps a short cache; counts calls against a daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: Pass a query and read the hits of the returned observation, each with a link a reader can check.
verdict_detail: openalex_semantic leads openalex_semantic_and_web (openalex_semantic_and_web 0.327 against openalex_semantic 0.347; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.664, 21 of 150 cases disagree); openalex_semantic is better than web_research (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=4.08e-06, 52 of 150 cases disagree)

name: act-in-the-world: the Body seat
description: Takes a goal with a written done-standard and tries to bring it about outside the model, by editing files, calling a write operation or running an agent, then reports whether the goal was met.
purpose: Make intended changes in the world and no unrequested ones, for any product that lets an AI act.
approach: Attempt the goal inside a bounded workspace, check it against its done-standard and report the result.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-act-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-act-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-act-in-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-act-in-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Intended changes made, no unrequested ones.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: A goal with a written done-standard, and a brief.
outputs: A DeepResult that says whether the goal was met, with the reason; it never raises.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.
verdict_detail: best guess, not yet significant: none 0.298 against fast_edit 0.972 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test; best guess, not yet significant: stream_json_goal_runner 0.938 against fast_edit 0.972 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test; best guess, not yet significant: subprocess_goal_runner 0.923 against fast_edit 0.972 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test

name: watch-for-risk: the Overseer seat
description: Watches a run and raises at most one small signal when a step cannot be undone or belongs to a person, and leaves ordinary work alone.
purpose: Stop irreversible or human-only steps before they happen, without slowing ordinary work, for any product that lets an AI act.
approach: Read a short digest of each step and signal proceed, redirect, answer now or escalate to a person.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-watch-for-risk has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-watch-for-risk has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-watch-for-risk chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Risks caught against false alarms, and latency.
parameters: The provider and model for the overseer arm, and the consumer's prompt as data.
inputs: A short digest of the run.
outputs: One signal: proceed, redirect, answer_now, escalate_deep or escalate_human; it never raises.
effects: At most one model call per step; none for the rule-based gate.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.
verdict_detail: consent_gate is better than none (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=2.29e-05, 18 of 36 cases disagree); consent_gate leads overseer (overseer 0.917 against consent_gate 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.5, 3 of 36 cases disagree); consent_gate leads two_stage (two_stage 0.944 against consent_gate 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.5, 2 of 36 cases disagree)

name: assemble-the-whole: the The whole being seat
description: Builds the whole mind from configuration in one call: each seat gets its selected arm, and a seat that needs something from the consumer says exactly what to pass.
purpose: Give any consumer a working system from one line of configuration.
approach: Resolve each seat's selected arm and its needs, build what can be built and report what is still pending.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-assemble-the-whole has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The production stage of metric-assemble-the-whole has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-assemble-the-whole chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: End-to-end pass rate on a production consumer.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: stay-current: the Learning seat
description: Names the areas whose research is older than the ninety day bar, so each can be researched again, compared and republished. The weekly research itself is run by the consumer's autopilot.
purpose: Keep every seat's candidates current for anyone who relies on the hub.
approach: Research each area again before its last research is 90 days old, compare the candidates and republish the result.
milestones: 1. Every seat's last_researched is inside the 90-day refresh window (metric-stay-current).
measures_of_success: Days since each seat was last researched and compared.
inputs: An ISO date (today when none is given).
outputs: The names of the registry's areas whose research is older than the ninety day bar on that date.
effects: Reads the registry's dated rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the weekly research is run by the consumer's autopilot.

name: read-registry-freshness: how old is each seat's research
description: Reads the date each area of the registry was last researched and reports its age against a 90 day bar, naming the stale areas.
purpose: Show maintainers which parts of the hub have gone stale.
approach: Read the recorded research dates and report the days since each.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-read-registry-freshness has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: Every area's research age is read correctly.
parameters: clock: optional, so a test can fix the date.
inputs: An ISO date, or the registry facts together with a consumer's connections.
outputs: Days since the date, or the combined freshness reading with the stale areas named.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: keep-it-generic: the Character seat
description: Audits the hub for consumer wording: the vendor-name branches in its own code, with how stale its research is and how much of it connects by configuration.
purpose: Keep the hub usable by any consumer, with no wording or settings of one product in it.
approach: Scan the hub for consumer-specific strings and keep prompts as data the consumer passes in.
milestones: 1. Consumer-specific strings found by the scan: none (metric-keep-it-generic).
measures_of_success: Consumer-specific strings found by scan (target 0).
outputs: Seats whose wording is data, whose arms are current and whose integrations are entries.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: connect-any-integration: the Hands seat
description: Reports how much of an area's hub connections are catalog entries that need no code, so an integration is added as data and never as code in the frontend, backend or runner.
purpose: Let users connect the apps they use with zero code per integration, for any product built on the hub.
approach: List integrations as catalog data from the hubs, connect them through one generic flow and expose their tools per user.
milestones: 1. A fake integration is added through the catalog alone and connects, calls a tool and disconnects with zero code changes. 2. At least two arms exist. 3. The selected arm was chosen by the seat's metric.
measures_of_success: Per-integration code changes in frontend, backend and runner (target 0 each); days from a hub listing an integration to a user connecting it (target at most 7); credential isolation checks all pass.
inputs: An area name (all areas when none is named).
outputs: The share, from 0 to 1, of the area's hub connections that need only configuration.
effects: Reads the registry's connection rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty. Design: see the review page hub-integrations-zero-code.

name: score-hub-connections: how much of an integration is a hub connection
description: Scores, per area, whether a hub is registered, how many of a consumer's connections need no code, and whether a fake hub is accepted by configuration alone.
purpose: Show a consumer how much of its integration is a hub connection and how much is hand-wired.
approach: Read the registry together with the consumer's binding and count connections per area.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-score-hub-connections has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: Zero-code connections and hand-wired services are counted correctly.
inputs: A consumer's Binding, or one registry fact and a kind of check.
outputs: Per-area checks and a combined score.
effects: None; it reads the registry files and the consumer's declared code paths.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: card-store: a place to keep and find cards
description: A small store that keeps cards, the hub's own memory unit, and finds them again by words or a tag.
purpose: Keep and find cards for any consumer, with no service to run.
approach: Store each card under its id and search by every word of the query.
milestones: 1. Every case passes: cards found again by words, nothing lost on a repeated add (metric-card-store).
measures_of_success: Cards found again by words; nothing lost on a second add of the same id.
parameters: The store location (in memory or one SQLite file).
inputs: A card to add, a card id, and a query with an optional tag and a result limit.
outputs: The id of an added card, a card or nothing for an id, the cards matching a query or a tag, whether a delete removed one, and the count.
effects: Writes and deletes cards in the store (a SQLite file when one is named); reads nothing else.
usage_notes: Default arm is local SQLite, in memory or one file.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: think-critically: the Critical thinking seat
description: Holds an answer to the evidence behind it and reports each claim the evidence does not support. Today the claim it checks is a link: every link in the answer must be in the evidence.
purpose: Check every answer and plan against its measure before it reaches a person.
approach: Name the problem, ideal and metric of each request, check the result against them, and retry when it falls short.
milestones: 1. The evidence check runs on written answers with and without supporting links. 2. A second arm exists beside it. 3. The selected arm was chosen by the seat's metric.
measures_of_success: Share of unsupported links in written answers that are reported, with no supported link reported.
outputs: The findings, one per claim the evidence does not support (an empty list when the answer held).
usage_notes: Pass the answer and the evidence text: critique(answer, evidence).

name: model-call: ask a model one question
description: One narrow call: a prompt at a tier in, text out. The hub builds it on call-a-model, so a consumer that wants a one-question model needs no object of its own.
purpose: Ask a model a question at the tier that fits, for any consumer.
approach: Send the prompt to the provider the hub assembled for the tier and return the text.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-model-call has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-model-call has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-model-call chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Answer returned for the tier asked; cost and time recorded by the caller.
parameters: The provider, or the consumer's own object.
outputs: The text a model answers to the prompt.
effects: One call to a model provider, which costs what the provider charges or draws on the operator's subscription.
usage_notes: No hub arm: the consumer provides the object.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: call-a-model: ask a vendor's model to plan, answer or list models
description: Plans, answers and lists models for one vendor, or for several through a router that steps to the next model when a provider fails.
purpose: Reach any model vendor through one interface, for any consumer that calls models.
approach: Wrap each vendor behind one interface and route each call to the provider that serves its model, with a fallback when it fails.
milestones: Arms for the main vendors and the Claude Code program, a router that fails over, and recorded failover and answer checks.
knowledge: Each vendor's SDK and the claude program have their own limits, listed beside the arm in the requirements table.
measures_of_success: A call is answered when the primary provider fails, and each vendor arm answers school maths problems correctly.
parameters: Per vendor: key, base url, options and fallback models, all constructor arguments; nothing is read from the environment.
inputs: A model id and a prompt, or a planning request.
outputs: Text, a plan or a list of models.
effects: Network calls to the vendor; token totals are kept per calling thread.
usage_notes: Name no model: the seat's selected arm answers. Pass arms= to choose another.
verdict_detail: multi_provider is better than single_provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=7.63e-06, 18 of 30 cases disagree)

name: remember-and-recall: the Subconscious, Intuition seat
description: Keeps what a person knows as cards and recalls the ones that bear on the task at hand, from the asker's own scope: the cards a context assembler names for the query, then the cards the store finds by its words.
purpose: Give an AI the context a task needs and nothing from another person's scope.
approach: Store knowledge as cards and admit it by relevance within the scope of the asker.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-remember-and-recall has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-remember-and-recall has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-remember-and-recall chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Right context admitted, nothing from another scope.
outputs: The cards a task needs, in one rendered view with their ids.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: context-assembler: pick the context a task needs
description: Selects the context a task needs from a store and renders it into one view, together with the ids of the cards it drew on.
purpose: Find the passages that bear on a request, for any consumer that keeps knowledge to draw on.
approach: Rank stored documents against the request by keywords, meaning or both, and return the top results.
milestones: BM25, vector, hybrid and composite arms with recorded runs on public retrieval sets.
knowledge: Retrieval quality depends on the corpus, so arms are compared on the same public and written queries.
measures_of_success: A relevant document is among the first five results.
parameters: The store and optional model provider the arm is built with, and the number of hits.
outputs: An assembled context view and the ids of the cards it drew on; it never raises.
usage_notes: Pass root= for the folder to index. With no root the corpus is empty and nothing is returned.
verdict_detail: bm25@analyzer=english leads bm25 (bm25 0.619 against bm25@analyzer=english 0.644; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.154, 16 of 323 cases disagree); bm25@analyzer=english leads vector (vector 0.635 against bm25@analyzer=english 0.644; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.78, 51 of 323 cases disagree)

name: cards-from-files: cards for a folder
description: Proposes a proportionate, current set of cards for material a consumer already keeps in files, without writing them.
purpose: Give any consumer cards for the knowledge it already keeps in files, so recall starts from what is there instead of an empty store.
approach: Group the files that belong together, describe each group, and report which cards an edit has made stale.
out_of_scope: Writing cards (the card store does) and choosing which cards a task sees (the context assembler does).
milestones: 1. The selected builder's balanced score on the pinned file-finding cases is at least the per-file floor's (metric-cards-from-files).
knowledge: Code graphs and repository maps group code by its call and import structure without a model; topic cards a model writes add the names a person would search for.
measures_of_success: The file a task needs is among the first files of the cards the fixed selector picks, at a price per build a team would pay, and no builder wins by putting many files in one card.
parameters: The model provider, for a builder that calls one.
inputs: A folder root, the list of files to read, and the cards already kept for it.
outputs: Cards in the card-store record shape (grouping, summary, keywords, files with their hashes), and the ids of kept cards whose files changed.
effects: Reads files; writes nothing (the caller writes through card-store).
usage_notes: Run it for a first index and after edits, passing the cards already kept so a builder skips covered files. The per-file builder is the free floor; a builder that calls a model has to buy its price in accuracy on the balanced score.
verdict_detail: per_file_symbols is better than graphify_files (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.55e-17, 63 of 63 cases disagree); per_file_symbols is better than llm_topic_cards (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=3.47e-17, 58 of 63 cases disagree); per_file_symbols is better than one_card (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.55e-17, 63 of 63 cases disagree); per_file_symbols is better than one_card_per_folder (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.55e-17, 63 of 63 cases disagree); per_file_symbols is better than two_cards (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=5.55e-17, 63 of 63 cases disagree)

name: search-backend: run one web search
description: One narrow call: a query in, a response of hits out. The hub ships thin adapters over open-source and hosted search services, and a consumer may provide its own.
purpose: Run a web search through any service, for any consumer that needs sources.
approach: Send the query to the chosen service and return hits with a title, a link and a snippet.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-search-backend has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The live stage of metric-search-backend has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-search-backend chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Result rows with a title, a link and a snippet for a query.
parameters: The service address or API key of the chosen arm, a timeout and an optional daily limit.
inputs: A query, a result limit and an optional instruction for a model-backed arm.
outputs: A response of hits (title, link, snippet, date, passages and their kind), an optional direct answer and the queries issued; raises SearchBackendError on failure.
effects: One network request per search to the chosen service, counted against the daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: The hub ships arms (searxng, serper, brave, tavily, gemini, provider) and a selector over them (hubofhubs.websearch.backends.select_search_backend). None is selected by default: no metric run exists yet, so a consumer names an arm in its selections or provides its own object.
verdict_detail: gemini is better than provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1.1e-05, 22 of 40 cases disagree)
